data.name: Ezekian
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Ezekian means 'God will strengthen'. In the Bible, Ezekiel, the name's biblical form, is the name of a prophet who was taken by God to Jerusalem and commissioned to prophesy to the Israelites. Ezekiel's visions and prophecies are recorded in the book of Ezekiel, which is part of the Old Testament. The name is also associated with the traditional Christian belief in divine guidance and strength.

in_hebrew.name: עזיקיאן
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עזיקיאן הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אלוהים יחזק אותי בקשרי אליו', נגזר מהשורש עזק, שפירושו 'לחזק' או 'לאזק', ומשמו של הנביא יחזקאל, שפירושו 'אלוהים יחזק'. השם עזיקיאן מופיע בתקופה של התחדשות רוחנית וקשר הדוק עם האל.

in_greek.name: Εζεκιάν
in_greek.long_meaning: Εζεκιάν σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός ενδυναμώνει τον άνθρωπον', προερχόμενο από τις ρίζες του εβραϊκού ονόματος יחזקאל (Ezechiel), που σημαίνει 'Deus confortabit' ή 'Dominus firmabit'. Ο προφήτης Ezekiel στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη έλαβε το όνομά του από το γεγονός ότι ο Θεός τον ενδυνάμωσε για το έργο του προφήτη.

in_latin.name: Ezekian
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Ezekian significat 'Deus confortabit hominem', derivatum ex hebraeo nomine יחזקאל (Iezekiel), quod interpretatur 'Deus confortabit' vel 'Dominus firmabit'. Propheta Ezekiel in Veteri Testamento hoc nomen accepit, quia Deus eum ad munus propheticum roboravit.

in_english.name: Ezekian
in_english.long_meaning: Ezekian is a Christian name derived from the Hebrew name יחזקאל (Ezechiel), meaning 'God will strengthen' or 'God will comfort'. It carries the spiritual significance of divine empowerment and reassurance. Historically, the name Ezekiel was borne by a major prophet in the Old Testament, known for his visions and messages of hope and restoration. The name Ezekian reflects a strong connection to faith and resilience.

historical_references.reference: In the early 6th century BCE, Ezekias was the king of Judah who successfully defended his kingdom against an invasion by king Sennacherib of Assyria, as recorded in the Bible's Old Testament books of Isaiah and II Kings.

historical_references.reference: Ezekias was also a contemporary and potential ally of king Hezekiah of Judah in the late 8th and early 7th centuries BCE. Hezekiah was known for his religious reforms and for rebuilding the Temple in Jerusalem, which was destroyed by the Assyrians in 701 BCE.
